_comment: Mutation measurement of the UI. Started as two files, picked so the run answers two different questions rather than producing one blended number; src/hooks/useFeatureToggle.js was added later because it writes a persisted admin setting and a mutant that inverted the value it posts, or dropped the failure branch, would leave a switch silently doing the opposite of what it shows. It runs against its own renderHook test, which touches nothing outside app/ui and so is safe in the sandbox. src/auth/usePermissions.js is the client-side permission gate: seven components import it, NO test file imported it before this pilot, and its 39% line coverage was incidental — whatever happened to execute while other components rendered. src/utils/matrixFilter.js is the opposite case: 99% coverage with its own dedicated test file, so its score says whether that number was earned. Enforced: see MUTATION FLOOR below. Run: cd app/ui && npm run test:mutation. MUTATOR SET: everything enabled, which is DELIBERATELY different from app/api/stryker.auth.config.json. There, StringLiteral and ObjectLiteral were disabled because permissions.js is largely a catalog of human-readable labels and mutating that prose produced 68 of 72 survivors while saying nothing about behaviour. Here the string literals ARE the behaviour: 'admin.auth' is the permission a hook checks for, and 'rows-as-resources' is a value the normaliser accepts — a wrong one silently grants or drops. Those mutants are worth killing, so they stay in. Do not copy the API's exclusions here without re-reading this. THE 10 REMAINING SURVIVORS ARE ANALYSED, NOT UNEXAMINED, and are left visible rather than declared away (the floor sits below the measured score, so they cost nothing): (a) 7 of them are the delimiters inside matrixFilter's `canonical()` -- '[' ',' ']' '{' ':' '}'. Both sides of any fingerprint comparison run through the SAME mutated serializer, so killing one needs two structurally different filters that collide once a delimiter is dropped. JSON.stringify escapes every string it emits, so the quote pattern needed to forge a collision cannot be produced by any value a filter can hold. (b) `Array.isArray(obj) -> false` serialises arrays as index-keyed objects; no filter field can hold either an array or a plain object depending on input (`list()` returns [] for a non-array, normalizeSort always returns an array), so the two shapes never meet in the same slot. (c) `typeof f === 'object' -> true` in normalizeMatrixFilter leaves `f ? f : EMPTY_FILTER`: a truthy non-object (string, number, boolean) has none of the sixteen filter fields on it, so every field falls back and the result is EMPTY_FILTER either way. (d) `permissions.size === 0 -> false` in usePermissions drops a redundant fast path -- an empty Set reaches `.some()` and returns false regardless. Re-check (a) and (b) if canonical() ever stops delegating to JSON.stringify. MUTATION FLOOR: `break` is set a few points under the measured score, and is a RATCHET — it only ever goes up. It is enforced by the weekly .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml (never on a PR: mutation is far heavier than the unit suite). The margin is not slack to spend, it absorbs the two things that legitimately move a score without anyone editing a test: a Stryker/vitest upgrade that changes which mutants are generated, and timeouts, which count as killed and can flip under CI load. Raise the floor when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green — a drop means a test stopped discriminating. Measured 95.6% when the floor was raised to 93. The shared crawler-wizard layer (saveCrawlerConfig + useCrawlerSave/useCredentialFields/useCrawlerDiscovery) joined at 97.1%, and useFeatureToggle.js sits at 100%; the ten analysed survivors below are unchanged and all belong to the original two files. SCOPE GREW FOR #1166 and the label 'permissions + filter' is now too narrow: this config is the UI's PURE-LOGIC scope — the modules that decide something, hold no JSX, and have their own dedicated test file. src/components/shared/sharedSnapshot.js and src/hooks/useHashPage.js joined on those terms. Both belong here rather than in the hooks configs specifically because their string literals ARE behaviour, which is the one thing that makes this config different: 'rotated' / 'rollup' / 'grid' / 'rows-as-subjects' are the values a share round-trips through the database, and 'dashboard' is the route a bare hash falls back to — a wrong one silently shows a recipient a different view than the sharer saw. Adding them costs the weekly run little: neither renders anything, so their mutants pay for two more small non-jsdom test files, not for a mount. Keep that admission test when adding a file here — a React component belongs in a mount-test-backed config or in the exclusions below, not in this one.

mutationExclusions.src/utils/crawlerMetaRegistry.js: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and this module resolves crawler metadata with import.meta.glob over ../../../tools/crawlers/*/CrawlerMeta.js — a path that does not exist in the sandbox. The glob would resolve to nothing there, so the dry run fails before a single mutant is evaluated (same constraint documented in vitest.stryker.config.js). Its selectors are unit-tested in src/utils/crawlerMetaRegistry.test.js — against injected fixtures for the branch logic AND against the real discovered registry, which is what catches an experimental flag being dropped from a CrawlerMeta.js.
mutationExclusions.src/components/CrawlersPage.SelectType.j: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and this module resolves crawler metadata with import.meta.glob over ../../../tools/crawlers/*/CrawlerMeta.js — a path that does not exist in the sandbox. The glob would resolve to nothing there, so the dry run fails before a single mutant is evaluated (same constraint documented in vitest.stryker.config.js). It imports crawlerMetaRegistry.js, so it inherits that. Presentational besides: its one decision (offer experimental types or not) is selectableCrawlerTypes(), mutation-relevant logic that lives in the excluded module above and is covered by CrawlersPage.SelectType.test.jsx mounting the real picker.
mutationExclusions.src/components/admin/ExperimentalFeature: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and this module resolves crawler metadata with import.meta.glob over ../../../tools/crawlers/*/CrawlerMeta.js — a path that does not exist in the sandbox. The glob would resolve to nothing there, so the dry run fails before a single mutant is evaluated (same constraint documented in vitest.stryker.config.js). It imports crawlerMetaRegistry.js, so it inherits that. Mounted end-to-end in ExperimentalFeaturesSection.test.jsx (flag rendering, both toggle directions, the failure path); the flag semantics it drives are mutation-tested server-side in app/api/stryker.features.config.json.
mutationExclusions.src/components/crawler/wizardFields.jsx: Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and the tests that assert this component's output are the crawler wizards' own render/e2e tests under tools/crawlers/, which is outside the sandbox — mutating it without its killers present would report false survivors, which is worse than measuring less (the same reasoning as vitest.stryker.config.js's narrow include). Presentational besides: labelled inputs, option lists, the schedule list and the Back/Next row. Its one behavioural rule — label and control stay siblings, because the e2e selects fields with `label:has-text("X") + input` — is asserted by those e2e tests, not by anything mutable here.
Cannot be mutated: Stryker sandboxes app/ui alone, and the tests that assert this component's output are the crawler wizards' own render/e2e tests under tools/crawlers/, which is outside the sandbox — mutating it without its killers present would report false survivors, which is worse than measuring less (the same reasoning as vitest.stryker.config.js's narrow include). The decision it encodes — which fields each auth method needs — is mirrored by buildCredentialFields/canSubmitCredentials in @ui/utils/crawlerCredentials, and THAT is unit-tested (credentialGating.test.js in the omada and midPoint folders) and mutable. This file only renders the result.
mutationExclusions.src/AppRoot.jsx: The root route dispatcher (#1166): one branch — a '#shared:<token>' hash renders the recipient shell, anything else renders App — wrapped in a Suspense fallback. Both halves of that branch are already mutation-tested as pure functions: parseSharedRoute in App.helpers.js and useHashPage.js, which is in the mutate list above. What is left in this file is the lazy() import and the fallback markup, so its mutants would measure JSX, not the routing decision. AppRoot.mount.test.jsx asserts both branches render.
mutationExclusions.src/contexts/SharedViewContext.jsx: A createContext(false) plus the one-line useContext reader that the shared shell flips to hide analyst-only affordances (#1166). There is no decision in the file to mutate — the only meaningful mutant is the default value, and SharedViewContext.mount.test.jsx pins that (a component outside the provider must see analyst chrome) along with each consumer's opt-out.
mutationExclusions.src/components/SharedMatricesPage.jsx: The Admin overview of every share (#1166): a fetch, a table of rows, and a revoke confirmation. Its only logic is formatting — 'Never opened' versus a usage count, Active versus Revoked — which is markup-adjacent text a mutant changes without changing behaviour. SharedMatricesPage.mount.test.jsx drives the list, the empty state and the revoke round-trip; the SQL behind it is contract-tested.
mutationExclusions.src/components/SharedMatrixPage.jsx: The recipient's shell (#1166): resolve the token, then render the matrix or one of the four terminal states. The two decisions it makes are extracted and covered elsewhere — applyDisplayMode (mutated above, in sharedSnapshot.js) folds the stored display mode back into the filter, and the HTTP-status-to-state mapping is asserted per status in SharedMatrixPage.mount.test.jsx. The rest is the bare chrome itself.
mutationExclusions.src/components/inputs/PeoplePicker.jsx: The directory typeahead behind 'Share with' (#1166). Its rules are asserted by inputs that discriminate in PeoplePicker.mount.test.jsx: a row with no sign-in name is offered but disabled, an already-picked person cannot be added twice, removal is by sign-in key, and an unsettled term reads as 'Searching…' rather than 'No people match'. Around those sits a debounced fetch and a chip list, so mutating the file measures mostly Tailwind classes and placeholder prose.
A permission-gated toolbar button that opens a modal (#1166). The gate is useHasPermission('data.share'), which lives in src/auth/usePermissions.js and IS mutated by this config; what remains here is `if (!canShare || !filter) return null` plus the open/closed state. Both are asserted in ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx (offered with the permission, absent without it, absent with no filter, and the click that opens the dialog) and again in SharedViewContext.mount.test.jsx, which pins that the button disappears inside a recipient's shell.
Chrome only (#1166): a Modal whose title and footer label flip once a share exists, wrapping ShareMatrixForm. Everything a share IS lives in that form, deliberately, so the toolbar and the wizard cannot drift. The one branch here (before/after creation) is asserted in ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/ShareMatrixForm.js: The body of 'share this matrix' (#1166). Its two decisions are asserted directly in ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx — the button stays disabled until the share has both a name and at least one recipient, and the POST body carries the filter, the managed toggle, the display mode from displayModeOf (mutated above) and the picked people. The server re-checks the recipient rule in shareRecipients.js, which is mutation-tested in app/api. The remainder is the shown-once link and its copy affordance.
mutationExclusions.src/components/matrix/WizardShareStep.js: A heading, a paragraph explaining that the step is optional, and ShareMatrixForm (#1166). No branches and no state — the file exists so the wizard's last step and the toolbar dialog render the same form. ShareMatrixDialog.mount.test.jsx asserts the two hosts offer the same controls.
mutationExclusions.src/components/shared/SharedMatrixHeader: Presentational header for the recipient's shell (#1166): the product mark, the share's name and a 'Shared matrix' label, with a Back control when a drill-down is open. No data and no decision — the back affordance's behaviour is asserted from the page in SharedMatrixPage.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/shared/SharedMatrixRow.js: One row of the Shared matrices table (#1166) — name, recipients, usage and the Revoke control, all rendered from props the page already resolved. Mutating it measures date and count formatting; what the row must SAY for a never-opened and for a revoked share is asserted in SharedMatricesPage.mount.test.jsx.
mutationExclusions.src/components/shared/SharedMatrixUnavai: Four static messages for a share that cannot be opened — revoked, unknown, not-for-you, failed (#1166) — and a lookup into that table. The file is deliberately prose: the recipient is a business user who must never see a status code. Mutating the strings would produce survivors that say nothing, which is exactly the permissions.js lesson recorded in the API's auth config.
